Prevention: Long rotations of six years or more are necessary to keep inoculum from building up in the soil during the winter season.
Fusarium wilt may be seed borne.
Inspect seedlings for symptoms of fusarium wilt.
Use new transplant trays or sanitize trays well.
Do not save seed from fields where
Avoid flood irrigation to prevent spreading of the disease.
Follow drip irrigation to prevent the disease spreading.
Monitoring: Symptoms include damping off in seedling from infested fields.
Wilting and chlorosis symptoms visible in older leaves.
Wilt is most evident in the heat of the day (afternoon hours).
Stem cracks and brown streaks often appear near the crown of the plant.
Direct Control: Pseudomonas fluorescence at 2.5 kg/Ha along with 50 kg
FYM (sieved) and 100 kg neem cake before last ploughing.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
Carbendazim at 1 g/l of water and 5-10 ml per plant.
